text: Writing clean code is an essential skill for every programmer. The most important goal is to make your code as readable as possible, not just for the computer, but for other humans who will read it later. This means using clear naming conventions; for example, a variable called `totalPrice` is far better than `tp` or `x`. Instead of writing one long block of complex logic, you should break your program into small, focused functions. Each function should do only one thing, and its name should clearly describe that action. This approach makes your code much easier to test and debug. Ultimately, clean code leads to better maintainability, allowing you and your team to update and fix software quickly and safely over time.
